mifid_ii_transaction_report_validator.text:
`mifid_ii_post_trade_transparency` answers the question "does this trade qualify for deferred publication, or should it be published near real-time?" It takes `trade_size`, `delayed_publication_threshold` and optionally `is_liquid`. Deferral applies when the size meets the threshold or the instrument is not liquid.

`mifid_ii_transaction_report_validator` answers a different question: "is this transaction report filled in properly?" It takes a `report` mapping of field names to values and checks that required fields are present and basically valid, such as LEI length, ISIN length, and positive price and quantity. It covers a core subset of 9 fields, not the full set of RTS 22 mandatory fields.

In short, one assesses publication timing for a trade, and the other checks the data quality of a report about it.

explain.text: `mifid_ii_post_trade_transparency` (MiFID II Post Trade Transparency) assesses whether a trade may qualify for deferred publication under MiFID II post-trade rules, or whether it should be published near real-time. You give it the executed `trade_size`, a `delayed_publication_threshold` for the size cutoff, and optionally `is_liquid`, which defaults to true. Deferral is flagged when the trade size is at or above the threshold, or when the instrument is not liquid. Otherwise, publication is near real-time. It is an assessment of the logic, not a ruling on what you must report.

when.text:
`mifid_ii_post_trade_transparency` (MiFID II Post Trade Transparency) fits when you need to check whether a trade may qualify for deferred publication or should be published near real-time.

- You have an executed trade and want to compare its size (`trade_size`) against a deferral size threshold (`delayed_publication_threshold`).
- You're dealing with an instrument that has no liquid market, so you'd set `is_liquid` to false. Deferral can then apply even when the trade is below the threshold.
- You want a quick, repeatable check across several trades, using the same threshold each time.
- Your instrument is liquid and the trade is below the threshold, and you want to confirm that near-real-time publication applies.
